newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian investors still fear U.S. correction.
newsitem.headline: Belgian investors still fear U.S. correction.

text.p: The Brussels bourse closed down as investors took a cautious line on Thursday despite favourable U.S. retail sales and CPI figures, and early gains in neigbouring bourses.

Dealers said buyers remained unsure whether the Dow was about to suffer from a major correction. "Confidence must first be restored in the market before we can see any big rises," Geert De Mesure at brokerage Delen & Co said.
The Bel-20 ended down 0.46 percent or 8.57 points at 1,862.98 after touching a high of 1,867.75. Volume of Belgian shares traded was a moderate 2.55 billion francs.
Investors were also selling stocks today ahead of Friday's settling of accounts.
"Everybody is now cautious and wants to secure their profits," said a dealer.
"We are still suffering from the lower dollar and the Bel-20 falls are linked to individual stocks," De Mesure said.
He added that "the big losers were BBL, with Petrofina suffering from lower oil prices".
Bank BBL fell 90 francs to 6,500. Petrofina shed 110 francs to 9,990 francs after having touched a year high at 10,750 on December 5.
Tractebel's board said after the close that it had asked three banks to look closer into the benefits of a full merger with its internatioal energy unit Powerfin.

They added there would be no final decision on whether to merge or not until the banks had concluded their findings and the 1996 annual accounts completed. Tractebel rose 50 francs to 14,575 ahead of the news. Powerfin closed up 30 francs to 4,850.
Electronics firm Barco which is set to enter the bourse on December 20 fell 0.7 percent to 5,400 francs, after news that Asphales is reducing its 4.11 percent stake.
